summary: LAGRANGE is an interactive lunar landing-site planning tool that ranks candidate landing locations according to mission requirements such as slope, roughness, landing-area size, crater hazards, sunlight preference, vehicle type, and risk tolerance. Users define a mission region and constraints, then receive ranked candidate sites with scores, evidence, explanations, and GeoJSON landing footprints. Results are displayed on an interactive 3D Moon with selectable markers and plan-view footprints. The system combines a React/TypeScript visualization interface with a FastAPI geospatial analysis backend. It is designed to help mission planners explore trade-offs transparently and identify promising locations before detailed engineering analysis. Current demo results use a clearly labelled synthetic South Pole terrain fixture and are not flight guidance.
details:
LAGRANGE lets users define a lunar mission region, landing-pad diameter, maximum slope, roughness limit, crater avoidance preference, sunlight preference, vehicle type, and risk tolerance. The frontend sends the mission request to a FastAPI backend. The backend evaluates elevation-derived slope, terrain roughness, crater hazards, valid landing footprints, and illumination proxies. Candidates that fail hard constraints are rejected; valid candidates are scored, ranked, and returned with confidence information, quality flags, explanations, coordinates, and GeoJSON footprints.

The React and TypeScript frontend presents the results as ranked cards, interactive 3D Moon markers, and landing-footprint visualizations. The backend uses Python, FastAPI, NumPy, Rasterio, and geospatial processing. The project is creative because it combines mission planning with an accessible visual interface and exposes why each location was ranked rather than presenting an unexplained score.

The current public demonstration uses a deterministic synthetic South Pole terrain dataset for development and testing. It is explicitly labelled as synthetic and must not be used for real landing decisions. NASA terrain datasets such as LOLA and LROC are planned sources for future scientific deployment.
